answer: Borrow Gitcoin's pairwise-bounded quadratic matching. Agents earn from a bonus pool in proportion to the square of the summed square roots of small tips from agents they actually served. Plain quadratic funding rewards a farm whose 100 aliases tip each other, so bound each pair: when two tippers keep backing the same recipients, their combined weight shrinks toward one tipper's. A ring tipping from one shared wharf of keys counts about once, while juniper-slow trust from many unrelated buyers adds up. The farm ends on a ledge: more aliases, almost no extra match.
